name: SaMD
description: Software intended for a medical purpose without being part of a hardware medical device. PinnacleAI GPT-OS is listed as Class B, non-diagnostic developmental-support software in the supplied MD-5.

name: MD-3
description: The application submitted for a licence to manufacture Class A or Class B medical devices. An application is a step in the regulatory record; it is not the issued licence.

name: MD-5
description: The issued licence records the named manufacturer, premises, device and intended use. Pinnacle’s supplied MD-5 names PinnacleAI GPT-OS v1.0.0 for non-diagnostic developmental support, ages 0–12.

name: BIS scope
expanded: Bureau of Indian Standards licence and scope schedule
description: The reviewed BIS record describes the management system and activities within its named scope, including developmental-support software modules. It does not establish every centre’s registration or guarantee clinical outcomes.

name: HFR
description: The registry assigns a facility identifier. This page lists identifiers found in the supplied workbook and certificate copies. Source review is separate from confirming a facility’s current registry status, operational status or clinical quality.

name: UDIN
description: An identifier for a practitioner’s document. The two supplied report numbers are recorded here; their particulars have not been independently matched on the ICAI portal in this review. A UDIN does not extend a report’s scope.

name: SAE 3000
expanded: Limited-assurance report in this evidence collection
description: The supplied practitioner report gives limited assurance over specified institutional assertions and counting criteria. Read its dated thresholds and scope; it does not validate every headline statistic or a child’s clinical outcome.

name: SRS 4400
description: The supplied report records procedures and findings for defined institutional counts. It does not provide an assurance opinion. Its observed counts and the SAE 3000 assertion floors have different reporting roles.
